recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. If stale generated diagrams are addressed later, handle them as a separate build/artifact-maintenance task rather than as a semantic FHIR-32365 fix.
issue_request: FHIR-32365 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 and requested an overall date period for MedicationRequest so implementations with multiple dosageInstruction periods would not need to derive the overall therapy span from every dosage line. The resolution called for effectiveDosePeriod 0..1 plus a dosage-instruction grouping containing renderedDosageInstruction, effectiveDosePeriod, and dosageInstruction.
initial_application: Commit 4af0fbee92667f2c92e676367bdbc834f3b8baa6 applied FHIR-32365 with FHIR-32488 by adding a MedicationRequest dose backbone containing renderedDosageInstruction, effectiveDosePeriod, and dosageInstruction.
additional_context: Later Applied issue FHIR-52888 changed MedicationRequest.effectiveDosePeriod to MedicationRequest.effectiveTiming[x] with Duration, Range, and Period choices, and source/fhir.ini maps the R5 effectiveDosePeriod to the current element. Subsequent DosageDetails work moved rendered dosage instruction content into the active DosageDetails data type used by MedicationRequest.dosageInstruction.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active StructureDefinition defines MedicationRequest.effectiveTiming[x] as the period over which the medication is taken and explicitly says that for multiple dosageInstruction lines it represents the earliest date and latest end date. No authoritative source edit is needed for FHIR-32365.

related_jiras.note: Applied later Pharmacy decision broadened and renamed MedicationRequest.effectiveDosePeriod to effectiveTiming[x] while preserving the overall dose-period semantics.
Later DosageDetails work made renderedInstruction required after rendered dosage instruction content moved out of MedicationRequest.
Later DosageDetails refinement did not change the FHIR-32365 overall-period conclusion.
